items.headline: NSW Chief Psychiatrist's review of the psychiatric impairment tool sits upstream of the psychological thresholds just raised
items.summary: A review by the NSW Chief Psychiatrist of the Psychiatric Impairment Rating Scale (PIRS) — the instrument used to assess permanent impairment for psychological and psychiatric injuries — is underway, mandated by the reform legislation to report within 18 months of assent (delivering into 2027). The review is tasked with judging whether PIRS is reliable, consistent and appropriate for measuring whole person impairment and whether an alternative approach should replace it.
items.so_what: The reform package has just lifted the psychological WPI threshold for extended weekly payments and lump sums to 25% (rising to 28% by 2029), so the measuring instrument behind those gateways is now doing far more work; any recommendation to revise or replace PIRS would change how many psychological claims actually clear the higher thresholds, making this a slow-burn but structurally significant signal for insurers pricing and reserving under the new settings. Worth carrying as a watch item as the 2027 reporting window approaches.
